title: Copilot Studio: block maker-provided credentials for tool authentication

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Held. The admin paths and the roadmap facts check out, but the page misstates what happens to agents already using maker credentials: Microsoft says every tool switches to end-user sign-in the moment the setting is saved, and that scheduled or autonomous agents then fail with no documented workaround, while the page says existing agents keep working until edited and that service identities are an escape route. It also states that no licence is needed where the documentation is silent, and records the default state as on for a control that restricts nothing until an administrator configures it.

claims.claim: The maker credential setting is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments (or Environment groups) > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents > Control maker credential options.
claims.quote: On the side navigation, select Manage. Select Environments or Environment groups. ... select Settings on the top menu bar. Expand the Product section, and select Features. Scroll to the Copilot Studio agents section. Under Control maker credential options, select End-user credentials or Maker-provided credentials, or both.

claims.claim: No PowerShell, Microsoft Graph, Power Platform API or pac CLI route is documented for the Control maker credential options setting.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Control maker credential options environment setting PowerShell Power Platform API automate Copilot Studio agents'; opened configure-no-maker-authentication and settings-features#copilot-studio-agents. Only the admin centre steps are documented.

claims.claim: Environment Admin can set it for a single environment; Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator is needed for environment groups.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin permissions (Environment Admin for a single environment, or Power Platform Administrator/Global Admin for environment groups).

claims.claim: The sharing control is at Power Platform admin center > Security > Threat detection > Sharing agent with embedded maker credentials > Set up, with scope environment group.
claims.quote: On the navigation pane, select Security, and then select Threat detection. Select Sharing agent with embedded maker credentials. A panel opens. ... Select Set up. ... You can configure the setting for an individual environment or an environment group.
claims.fix: Add a note that this control is in preview (the cited page is headed 'Control sharing agents with embedded maker credentials (preview)' and marked prerelease), and widen the scope: the page configures it per environment or per environment group, and a second Learn page gives the per-environment path Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Features > Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials with modes 'All sharing allowed' and 'Safe sharing enforced' (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/configure-sharing-agents-embedded-maker-credentials). Cite it.

claims.claim: No API or script route is documented for the sharing control.
claims.quote: Searched: 'sharing agents with embedded maker credentials setting PowerShell API environment group rule'; opened control-sharing-agents-with-embedded-maker-credentials, configure-sharing-agents-embedded-maker-credentials and settings-features#copilot-studio-agents. All three give admin centre steps only.

claims.claim: A maker picks the credential for a tool at Copilot Studio > Tools > tool > Details > Additional details > Authentication.
claims.quote: Go to the Tools page for your agent, and select the tool from the list of tools. ... Details ... Additional details: ... Authentication: Select whether to use the user's (End user) or maker's (Maker-provided) credentials for the tool. By default, user authentication applies.

claims.claim: No API route is documented for the per-tool credential choice.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio tool authentication end user credentials maker-provided set programmatically API Dataverse'; the results were the maker UI pages (add-tools-custom-agent, configure-enduser-authentication, security-scan, configure-no-maker-authentication). None documents an API.

claims.claim: Agents that already use maker-provided credentials keep working until the tool is edited; the admin setting removes options from the maker's list rather than overriding a saved choice.
claims.quote: All tools for all agents in the impacted environments instantly change to require end-user credentials at runtime. ... Once active, all existing and new agents in that environment adhere to this rule. ... If the maker previously had a tool configured with their credentials, they might be prompted to change it before publishing the agent.
claims.fix: Replace both statements: once the setting is saved, every tool in every existing and new agent in the environment requires end-user credentials at run time, and a maker whose tool is still configured for their own credentials may be prompted to change it before publishing (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/configure-no-maker-authentication).

claims.claim: The default state is 'on'.
claims.quote: Page: 'By default, both End-user and Maker-provided credentials are enabled.' | Front matter: defaultState on. The standard's default state for a feature that is itself a control is admin-opt-in when the sources say it restricts nothing until an admin configures it.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to admin-opt-in: the setting restricts nothing until an administrator changes it. Then reconsider action: act-now rested on 'on by default'; with status In development and nothing enforced by default, prepare fits the standard's definition.

claims.claim: The allowed values are end-user credentials, maker-provided credentials, or both, and the default is both.
claims.quote: select End-user credentials or Maker-provided credentials, or both. ... By default, both End-user and Maker-provided credentials are enabled.

claims.claim: The setting applies per environment or per environment group; environments in a group inherit the group setting and cannot be configured individually.
claims.quote: You can't configure this feature on the individual details page for environments that are in a group, you must use the group's details page. ... environment group settings override any environment settings.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Environment-group configuration needs Managed Environments.
claims.quote: Environment groups can only contain managed environments.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/environment-groups for the Managed Environments requirement; none of the cited pages states it.

claims.claim: Configuring an environment group needs a tenant admin role.
claims.quote: If the environment you want to configure is part of an environment group, you must be a tenant admin with access to the group.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No additional licence is required for the control itself.
claims.quote: Searched: the cited page's Prerequisites section lists 'Power Platform admin permissions' and nothing else; no Microsoft page read states that the setting needs no licence, and 'Managed Environments licensing' pages speak only to managed environments.
claims.fix: Replace 'No additional licence for the control' and 'No licence cost for the setting itself' with the narrower statement the page supports: the setting's prerequisites list Power Platform admin permissions and name no licence (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/configure-no-maker-authentication#prerequisites).

claims.claim: Managed Environments needs standalone Power Platform or Copilot Studio licences for the users of those environments.
claims.quote: When you activate managed environments in an environment, all active usage requires one of these standalone licenses or pay-as-you-go meters.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/managed-environment-licensing and add that pay-as-you-go meters for Power Apps per app, Power Pages and Copilot Studio also qualify.

claims.claim: Removing the maker-provided option applies immediately: all tools switch to end-user credentials at run time, makers lose the option in the authoring UI, and Microsoft's documentation warns to prepare makers and users because the next conversation prompts for sign-in.
claims.quote: the feature immediately turns off the maker's ability to select their credentials for authenticating tools within the environment or environment group. All tools for all agents in the impacted environments instantly change to require end-user credentials at runtime. You should prepare your makers and users for this change, as any new conversations with the impacted agents prompts the agent user for their sign-in details for the connected service.

claims.where: What's changing; front matter: status, targetDate, previewDate
claims.claim: Public preview was September 2025, the General Availability target is August 2026 and the roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: status: In development; targetDate: August CY2026; previewDate: September CY2025; releasePhase: General Availability, Preview

claims.claim: The admin centre setting is documented and available while the roadmap still reads In development.
claims.quote: Admins can enable and disable the selection of maker-provided credentials in the Power Platform admin center, as described in this article.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Copilot Studio's automatic security scan warns makers before publishing when a tool uses maker-provided credentials.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio automatically runs a security scan and warns makers before publishing. ... The maker selects Maker-provided credentials option under Credentials to use for connectors and flows. ... the security scan provides a warning if the maker changes it to Maker-provided credentials.

claims.claim: With end-user credentials enforced, Purview audit records are attributable to the right person.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio audit logs Purview tool actions attributed to end user when end-user credentials used'; opened purview/ai-copilot-studio and purview/audit-copilot. They describe audit records of prompts and responses and who interacted with the agent; none states how tool actions are attributed under end-user versus maker credentials.
claims.fix: Remove 'which also makes Purview audit records attributable to the right person', or cite a Microsoft page that states how Copilot Studio audit records attribute tool actions.

claims.claim: Enforcing end-user credentials means stored maker connections are no longer used at run time.
claims.quote: No stored maker credentials are used at run time, aligning the agent's behavior with the end user's actual permissions.

claims.claim: Blocking maker credentials breaks autonomous agents unless they use system identities or the run-only sharing model where each user supplies connections.
claims.quote: When maker-provided credentials are prevented from being used, agents require real-time user interaction because each tool call must be authenticated with a live user sign-in. As a result, agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events, or that attempt to run in the background, fail due to missing credentials. All agent triggers must involve an active user.
claims.fix: Replace with: when maker-provided credentials are blocked, agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events, or that run in the background, fail because every tool call needs a live user sign-in, and Microsoft documents no exception for system identities or run-only sharing (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/configure-no-maker-authentication#scope-of-enforcement-and-experience).

claims.claim: Agents that need a service identity can move to a service principal, API key or managed identity connection under this setting.
claims.quote: Searched: configure-no-maker-authentication documents only End-user and Maker-provided credentials and says all agent triggers must involve an active user; configure-sharing-agents-embedded-maker-credentials names service principals, API keys and managed identities only as connection types to review before enabling the sharing control.
claims.fix: Remove the advice, or move it to Open questions: no page read documents a non-user credential type that stays available once maker-provided credentials are blocked.

claims.claim: Flows called from agents that use maker-only credentials fail until reconfigured.
claims.quote: The control over the authentication type covers connectors, built-in actions, and embedded Power Automate flows equally. A Power Automate flow as a tool in the agent also requires each user to sign in for any connections that flow uses.
claims.fix: Replace with: flows used as tools are covered in the same way, and each user is prompted to sign in for the connections the flow uses (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/configure-no-maker-authentication#scope-of-enforcement-and-experience).

claims.claim: The item is Worldwide (standard multi-tenant) only and no government cloud dates are published.
claims.quote: clouds: Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)

claims.claim: The control affects connectors, flows and MCP tools that offer a credential choice.
claims.quote: The control over the authentication type covers connectors, built-in actions, and embedded Power Automate flows equally.
claims.fix: List what the page lists: connectors, built-in actions and embedded Power Automate flows. MCP tools are not named on the page; the tools page says only that an MCP server's Details section is similar to other tools (https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/add-tools-custom-agent).

claims.claim: Knowledge sources follow their own authentication model.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio knowledge sources authentication end user maker credentials SharePoint knowledge agent author authentication'; knowledge-add-sharepoint says generative answers run on behalf of the chatting user under the agent's authentication settings, but no page read relates knowledge-source authentication to the Control maker credential options setting.
claims.fix: Remove the sentence, or cite a Microsoft page that states how knowledge-source authentication behaves when maker-provided credentials are blocked.

claims.claim: Maker guidelines and maker welcome content can be set in the Power Platform admin center to publish the change to makers.
claims.quote: 13 Maker guidelines (preview) | 14 Maker welcome content

claims.claim: Copilot Studio agent status surfaces tools configured with maker-provided credentials.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio surfaces connection-sharing violations in Agent status. For an authenticated agent that you didn't share, a warning appears indicating how many connections violate the administrator's connection-sharing policy.
claims.fix: Say that Agent status reports connection-sharing policy violations when the sharing control is enforced, and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-sharing-controls-limits; the security scan is what warns about maker-provided credentials generally.

claims.claim: Admins can stop makers choosing their own credentials for tools, forcing end-user authentication.
claims.quote: The Control maker credential options feature enables this by letting you control how a maker can authenticate tools in an agent. You choose whether makers can select to use their own credentials for authenticating tool connections, to use the end-user's credentials, or to have access to both.

claims.claim: A companion control blocks sharing of agents that still rely on maker connections.
claims.quote: Administrators can prevent makers from sharing or publishing Copilot Studio agents that expose a connection with maker-provided credentials to end users when the connection isn't safe to share.

claims.claim: The cited pages security-scan, guidance/sec-gov-phase3 and add-tools-custom-agent exist and support what the page attributes to them.
claims.quote: Secure your Copilot Studio projects ... Apply restrictive data policies to your environment ... Using managed environment features requires Copilot Studio agents to be built in or deployed within a managed environment. (All three pages opened; the pre-check's fetch failures were the checker's network, not missing pages.)
